study_strategy.family_look_here_first: First decide what kind of flower head you are seeing: radiate head with rays + disk, or discoid head with disk florets only. Then inspect leaf arrangement, phyllaries, pappus, and head architecture instead of relying on flower color.

quick_key.if: opposite triangular 3-veined leaves + blue-violet flat-topped all-disk heads
narrow rough leaves + usually one radiate head with drooping rays around a prickly cone
alternate petiolate resinous leaves + rounded cluster of many small pink-purple all-disk heads
opposite broad coarse-toothed 3-veined leaves + white flat-topped all-disk heads

family_traits: apparent flower is a capitulum/head composed of many small florets
head subtended by an involucre of phyllaries
heads may be radiate, discoid, ligulate, or other specialized forms
anthers form a tube around the style in typical Asteraceae flowers
inferior ovary produces a one-seeded cypsela
calyx is commonly modified into a pappus of bristles, scales, awns, or may be reduced
priority_comparisons: Conoclinium coelestinum vs Ageratina altissima — same all-disk/flat-top architecture, distinguish leaf form + head color/scale
Echinacea angustifolia vs Ratibida columnifera — prickly broad cone + narrow entire leaves vs elongated column + divided leaves
Pluchea camphorata vs Heterotheca subaxillaris — pink-purple discoid heads vs yellow radiate heads despite shared 'camphorweed' common name
